# Linux Distro Picker

The complete text content of the Linux Distro Picker website.

## Homepage

Linux Distro Picker is an interactive tool that helps you find the best Linux distribution for your needs. Answer questions about gaming, development, user-friendliness and more to get personalized recommendations. The app includes a quick quiz, a filterable grid of distributions (filter by purpose and release model), detailed per-distribution information, and a like/favorites system. Supports English and Belarusian and features dark and light themes.

Why use Linux? Linux is a free, open-source operating system family. As of mid-2026 there are approximately 100-120 million computers and 60-75 million Linux users worldwide (around 25-30% of whom use Ubuntu, 10% Linux Mint, 5% Arch Linux, and 4% Debian), representing about 4-5% of the market share.

The app intentionally covers a hand-picked set of distributions that are good for beginners, and is not a database of all existing Linux distributions. It purposefully excludes enterprise-level distributions (Red Hat, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux), niche distributions (Kali, Alpine), and distributions aimed at experienced users (Arch Linux, Ubuntu, Debian, NixOS, Gentoo, Void, Artix, Slackware, MX Linux, Manjaro, elementaryOS, Solus) to keep the choice simple. In the end of the day, most Linux distributions share the same technologies and are very similar.

Dual-booting hints: install Linux on a separate disk and don't use Windows tools to resize partitions on it, as Windows can make Linux unbootable. If a distribution does not support Secure Boot, turn Secure Boot off in the BIOS before installing it.

Recommended software: browsers — Brave (privacy and ad blocking), Helium (performance and minimalism), Zen (design and vertical tabs), Floorp (customizability); office — OnlyOffice, LibreOffice; torrent client — qBittorrent; disk analyzer — Filelight (KDE/Qt), Baobab (GNOME/GTK), gdu (Rust CLI); local AI — LM Studio (Mistral model recommended); extended software support — Flatpak, Distrobox; running Windows apps — Bottles; cleaners — BleachBit, Stacer; system backup — Timeshift.

## Distributions


### Linux Mint

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/mint

Been here for quite a while. Community-driven, stable and familiar. The main edition features the Cinnamon desktop environment. A general-purpose distro, can be used for gaming too (like most distros), but it doesn't come with special tools pre-installed. Works well even on 10-15 years old computers. For older computers (for instance, those with only 2–4 GB of RAM), the Xfce edition of Linux Mint is recommended.

Key facts:
- Based on: Ubuntu
- Desktop environment(s): Cinnamon, MATE, Xfce
- Beginner-friendly: 5/5
- Userbase: ~3-10 million
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: Swap file
- Official website: https://linuxmint.com/

Highlights:
- Extremely polished and intuitive desktop
- Strives to have GUI apps for everything to eliminate the need of using the terminal, like for example Driver Manager
- May look old-style

### Zorin OS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/zorin

A polished distro focused on visual appeal and ease of use, featuring the GNOME desktop environment with 3D animations and various out-of-the-box layouts. Similar hardware requirements to Linux Mint.

Key facts:
- Based on: Ubuntu
- Desktop environment(s): GNOME
- Beginner-friendly: 5/5
- Userbase: ~2 million
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: Swap file
- Official website: https://zorinos.com/

Highlights:
- Sleek design
- Good even for people that have no idea what Linux is

### Pop!_OS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/popos

Built by System76, featuring the COSMIC desktop environment (macOS-like) and focusing on usability. Has tiling window support. Good for creative work and productivity, but not an ideal choice for gaming, as its package versions considerably lag behind their latest releases and the COSMIC desktop environment is relatively new. However, Flatpaks partially resolve this issue as they are updated frequently and independantly of the standard system repositories.

Key facts:
- Based on: Ubuntu
- Desktop environment(s): COSMIC
- Beginner-friendly: 5/5
- Userbase: ~1-2 million
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: zRAM + Swap Partition
- Official website: https://pop.system76.com/

Highlights:
- Innovative design with tiling window capability
- Not up-to-date software

### Kubuntu

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/kubuntu

A well-established and trusted distro, based on Ubuntu with the KDE Plasma desktop environment (the most feature-rich). It is backed by a huge corporation, Canonical. Similar hardware requirements to Linux Mint.

Key facts:
- Based on: Ubuntu
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma
- Beginner-friendly: 4.8/5
- Userbase: ~1 million
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: Swap file
- Official website: https://kubuntu.org/

Highlights:
- Has a lot of documentation available
- Uses Snap packages

### Tuxedo OS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/tuxedo

Tuxedo OS is a better Kubuntu alternative which is developed by TUXEDO Computers. It uses Flatpaks instead of Snaps, has a custom kernel, and includes other improvements. It is a semi-rolling distribution meaning it has newer software versions, including cutting-edge versions of KDE Plasma. Tuxedo OS comes pre-installed with the TUXEDO Control Center for managing fan speeds and power profiles, and it supports system snapshots with the help of the Btrfs filesystem. A good choice for gaming as well. Their mirrors can be slow for updates if you are very far away from Germany.

Key facts:
- Based on: Debian Testing
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma
- Beginner-friendly: 4.8/5
- Userbase: ~100k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: Swap file
- Official website: https://www.tuxedocomputers.com/en/TUXEDO-OS_1.tuxedo

Highlights:
- Full-fledged OS with up-to-date and stable software

### KDE Linux

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/kde-linux

An immutable (using Btrfs snapshots) Linux OS built by KDE. Immutability makes it extremely stable, but keeps the system read-only (which isn't a problem for most users). Strives to be as user-friendly as possible. Yet to be released, here just for information, don't install it just yet.

Key facts:
- Based on: independent
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma
- Beginner-friendly: 5/5
- Userbase: n/a
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: zRAM + Swap File
- Official website: https://kde.org/linux/

Highlights:
- Stable, modern, and reliable general-purpose OS

### openSUSE

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/openSUSE

openSUSE is a modern, general-purpose, stable, and reliable distribution intended for both professional and casual users. It is sponsored by SUSE, the first company to market Linux for the enterprise. It comes in two main variants: Tumbleweed (a rolling release) and Leap (a point release), and offers three primary desktop environments: KDE Plasma, GNOME, and Xfce (with more options available during installation). openSUSE greatly leverages the Btrfs filesystem by making snapshots of files and packages with Snapper to ensure system integrity. Also, historically, it used the YaST configuration tool to manage the entire system from a single place, but now it has been replaced with modern solutions. At its core, it's similar to Fedora but with a greater focus on system stability. It is a perfect choice for system administrators and regular users (yes, even gamers). The OS adheres strictly to open-source practices and therefore does not contain proprietary components by default.

Key facts:
- Based on: independent
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma, GNOME, Xfce, and more
- Beginner-friendly: 3.8/5
- Userbase: ~0.5-1 million
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: Swap partition
- Official website: https://www.opensuse.org/


### Fedora

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/fedora

Perfect for developers. Comes in many editions/spins, including one with the KDE Plasma desktop environment. It frequently updates apps and system components during its release cycle, keeping the software up-to-date while still remaining a point-release distribution. Fedora is a fully open-source project, so it doesn't come with Nvidia drivers or other proprietary software preinstalled.

Key facts:
- Based on: independent
- Desktop environment(s): GNOME, KDE Plasma, Xfce, Cinnamon, COSMIC, MATE, LXQt, LXDE, Budgie, and more
- Beginner-friendly: 4/5
- Userbase: ~1-2 million
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://fedoraproject.org/kde/

Highlights:
- Cutting-edge and reliable distribution

### Ultramarine

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/ultramarine

An out-of-the-box version of Fedora. It features extra repositories, multimedia codecs, and preinstalled Nvidia drivers — essentially everything most users would manually set up post-installation. The additional Terra repository with its cutting-edge software makes it a truly semi-rolling distro. Ultramarine to Fedora is what Ubuntu is to Debian. A good choice for gaming. Its developers also provide a conversion script allowing you to migrate from Fedora to Ultramarine Linux.

Key facts:
- Based on: Fedora
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma, GNOME, Xfce, Budgie
- Beginner-friendly: 4.8/5
- Userbase: ~2k
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://ultramarine-linux.org/

Highlights:
- Pre-configured distribution with up-to-date software

### EndeavourOS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/endeavouros

Arch Linux made easy. It provides a graphical installer and makes minimal changes to the base system.

Key facts:
- Based on: Arch Linux
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma, GNOME, Xfce, Cinnamon, MATE, LXQt, LXDE, Budgie, i3
- Beginner-friendly: 3/5
- Userbase: ~100k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: None
- Official website: https://endeavouros.com/

Highlights:
- Simple and powerful with no bloat
- A lot of available software in repositories
- Very fast boot and shutdown times
- Doesn't configure zRAM by default

### CachyOS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/cachyos

An Arch-based rolling distribution optimized for performance, featuring the KDE Plasma desktop environment (among many others). Though not initially gaming-ready, it can be easily set up for gaming by installing a single meta package (cachyos-gaming-meta). The handheld edition, on the other hand, is gaming-ready. Perfect for tech enthusiasts who want to have full control over their system. The extreme optimizations of CachyOS may result in lower stability compared to EndeavourOS.

Key facts:
- Based on: Arch Linux
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma, GNOME, COSMIC, Xfce, Niri, Hyprland, and more
- Beginner-friendly: 3.5/5
- Userbase: ~250-600k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://cachyos.org/

Highlights:
- Extreme performance optimizations
- A lot of community support
- Integrated snapshots with a dedicated boot menu

### Omarchy

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/omarchy

An opinionated Arch-based rolling distribution powered by the Hyprland tiling window manager and built for productivity in mind. Minimalistic UI and workflow, but it ships with some productivity software. The workflow revolves around using hotkeys and, optionally, AI agents. The UI is highly customizable, with a large database of community extensions.

Key facts:
- Based on: Arch Linux
- Desktop environment(s): Hyprland
- Beginner-friendly: 3/5
- Userbase: ~60-200k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://omarchy.org/

Highlights:
- Beautifully pre-configured setup with tiling workflow
- The system is complete which eliminates the need to manually tweak it
- A lot of stock themes
- A lot of productivity software pre-installed
- Very fast installation within minutes

### SteamOS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/steamos

An official gaming OS from Valve that powers Steam Deck, Steam Machine and other devices like Lenovo Legion Go. Immutable (using its own RAUC and desync technologies), user-friendly and optimized for gaming. Features the KDE Plasma desktop environment.

Key facts:
- Based on: independent
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma
- Beginner-friendly: 4.8/5
- Userbase: ~5-10 million
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: zRAM + Swap File
- Official website: https://store.steampowered.com/steamos


### Bazzite

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/bazzite

A gaming immutable (using OSTree) Linux distribution, perfect for both PCs and handhelds (has a special edition for them). A SteamOS alternative, but it has better desktop mode support. 16GB of RAM is recommended for Bazzite. Take a survey on the official website to see if your hardware supports the Linux gaming.

Key facts:
- Based on: Fedora Atomic
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma, GNOME
- Beginner-friendly: 5/5
- Userbase: ~100k
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://bazzite.gg/

Highlights:
- Universal gaming distro for desktop and handhelds
- May take up about 4-5Gb of RAM on idle

### Nobara

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/nobara

A gaming distro with a mutable core system, giving you full control. It was developed by the creator of Proton-GE, a utility at the heart of Linux gaming, and features both PC and handheld versions. Provides you the full power of Fedora, but comes with graphics drivers and gaming software preinstalled on top of that.

Key facts:
- Based on: Fedora
- Desktop environment(s): KDE Plasma, GNOME
- Beginner-friendly: 4.5/5
- Userbase: ~25k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://nobaraproject.org/

Highlights:
- Gaming distro that can be used for everything else too
- Good community support
- May have some update friction

### PikaOS

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/pikaos

A mutable gaming distribution. Similar to Nobara, but based on Debian (unstable branch with newer software). It offers you the option to install a gaming meta-package after the OS installation, meaning you can keep it bloat-free and configure it yourself. The GNOME edition features a layout switcher, just like Zorin OS.

Key facts:
- Based on: Debian Unstable
- Desktop environment(s): GNOME, KDE Plasma, COSMIC, Niri, Hyprland
- Beginner-friendly: 4.5/5
- Userbase: ~10k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: zRAM
- Official website: https://wiki.pika-os.com/home


### Lubuntu

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/lubuntu

A user-friendly lightweight Ubuntu variant, perfect for computers produced between 2004 and 2011 designed for Windows XP/Vista with only 2Gb of RAM. You can make it even faster if you use a native browser package (for instance, Brave) instead of the default Firefox Snap one and turn on zRAM (and give the Swap file the lowest priority).

Key facts:
- Based on: Ubuntu
- Desktop environment(s): LXQt
- Beginner-friendly: 4.8/5
- Userbase: ~100k
- Secure Boot support: Yes
- Swap strategy: Swap file
- Official website: https://lubuntu.me/


### antiX

URL: https://distro-picker.vercel.app/distro/antiX

Ultra light distro, requires as minimum as 256Mb of RAM to run (more to run apps smoothly). Suitable for ancient computers designed for Windows XP.

Key facts:
- Based on: Debian
- Desktop environment(s): Fluxbox, IceWM, JWM
- Beginner-friendly: 3.8/5
- Userbase: ~20k
- Secure Boot support: No
- Swap strategy: None
- Official website: https://antixlinux.com/
